label: Position name
summary: The name of the court position type, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as "Can be employed as [position] by [character]" and in the heading of the effects a position has on its employee.

label: Position name, plain
summary: The name of the court position type as plain text, without the hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the headings "[position] requirements:" and "Effect on [position]:". Going by its name, it is the same name as GetName but without the tooltip attached.

label: Courtiers hired by character
summary: A whole number taking one argument; going by its name, how many courtiers a given character has hired into this court position.
details: Vanilla texts and GUI files never use it. The game documents nothing more, so who the argument is and what is counted is a reading of the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the character whose hired courtiers are counted (from the name only).

label: Required rank
summary: Going by its name, the rank a character must have to hold this court position.
details: The game gives no return type for it and vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: Revoke cost text
summary: The cost of removing someone from this court position, as ready-made text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip line "Revocation cost: ..." for a court position.

label: Position tasks
summary: The list of tasks that belong to this court position, for a GUI list to show.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data for lists in the Great Steppe window and in the shared tooltip, and the tooltip hides its task section when the list is empty.

label: Position icon text
summary: Going by its name, the icon of the court position as an inline text icon.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other types with a function of the same name are used in texts to put an icon before a name, which only hints at the meaning here.

label: Position icon, unformatted
summary: Going by its name, the court position's inline text icon without the extra text formatting.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other types use a function of the same name next to a name in texts, which only hints at the meaning.

label: Auto-assign best
summary: Whether the given character has set this court position to be filled automatically with the highest-aptitude candidate when it falls vacant, if there is one.
details: Vanilla uses it as one line of the "When vacated:" list in the position tooltip, whose text reads "Auto-assign highest aptitude candidate, if available". Aptitude is how well a character suits the position.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose setting is checked.
fields.values: a character, vanilla passes the player

label: Auto-assign best or event
summary: Whether the given character has set this court position to be filled automatically with the highest-aptitude candidate, or else to be notified, when it falls vacant.
details: Vanilla uses it as one line of the "When vacated:" list in the position tooltip; that line says "Auto-assign highest aptitude candidate, or notify with ..." (the rest of the line is not in the input).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose setting is checked.
fields.values: a character, vanilla passes the player

label: No automation
summary: Whether the given character has no automation for this court position, so nothing happens by itself when it falls vacant.
details: Vanilla uses it for the "No automation" line of the "When vacated:" list in the position tooltip (a check mark when true). The court positions window shows a part only when it is false for the player.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose setting is checked.
fields.values: a character, vanilla passes the player

label: Auto: show event
summary: Whether the given character has set this court position so that an event suggests the best candidates when it falls vacant.
details: Vanilla uses it for the "Suggest best candidates in event" line of the "When vacated:" list in the position tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose setting is checked.
fields.values: a character, vanilla passes the player

label: Has custom liege modifiers
summary: Going by its name, whether the court position gives its liege (the employer) custom modifiers.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: Has employee modifiers
summary: Whether the court position gives modifiers to the character who holds it.
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared tooltip to show the paragraph "Effect on [position]:" with the employee modifiers only when it is true.

label: Has employee requirements
summary: Whether the court position has requirements a character must meet to hold it.
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared tooltip to show the requirements section only when it is true.

label: Has icon
summary: Going by its name, whether the court position has an icon.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other types have a function of the same name that the tooltip uses to show an icon only when there is one.

label: Has liege court modifiers
summary: Whether the court position gives modifiers to the court of the liege who employs the holder.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the matching section in the appoint window. The "court" part is read from the name.

label: Has liege modifiers
summary: Whether the court position gives modifiers to the liege who employs the holder.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the matching tooltip section, and the encyclopedia entry for a court position picks one of two texts by it.

label: Has liege requirements
summary: Whether the court position has requirements that the liege (the employer) must meet.
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared tooltip to show that section only when it is true.

label: Has no primary skill
summary: Whether the court position has no primary skill.
details: Vanilla uses it in the court positions window to show the part for positions without a skill. The primary skill is the skill the position is judged by, read from the name.

label: Has primary skill
summary: Whether the court position's primary skill is the one named.
details: Vanilla calls it with 'diplomacy', 'martial' and 'stewardship' in the court positions window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a skill name in quotes, such as 'diplomacy'

label: Has scaling liege court modifiers
summary: Going by its name, whether the position gives the liege's court modifiers that scale (grow with something, such as the holder).
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: Has scaling liege modifiers
summary: Going by its name, whether the position gives the liege modifiers that scale.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: Has static liege court modifiers
summary: Going by its name, whether the position gives the liege's court modifiers that stay fixed.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: Has static liege modifiers
summary: Going by its name, whether the position gives the liege modifiers that stay fixed.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: Has valid courtiers
summary: Whether the given character has courtiers who could fill this court position.
details: Vanilla uses it in the "no one to add" text of an empty position in the court positions window, together with a check whether the character can hire for the position at all.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose courtiers are checked.

label: Has visible tasks
summary: Going by its name, whether the court position has tasks that are shown to the given character.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the character the tasks are shown to (from the name only).

label: Is powerful agent
summary: Whether the court position is a powerful agent position.
details: Vanilla uses it in the court positions windows to show a part for such a position, for example when no character holds it yet. What makes a position a powerful agent is not given in the input.

label: Is shown
summary: Going by its name, whether the court position is shown to the given character.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other types have a function of the same name used for visibility, which only hints at the meaning.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the character it is shown to (from the name only).

label: Is travel related
summary: Whether the court position is related to travel.
details: Vanilla uses it in the appoint window to show a part for such positions.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether the court position exists (the reference points at a real position type).
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other types use a function of the same name to test a reference before using it, which only hints at the meaning.

label: Localize
summary: Going by its name, turns something into its localized text; it takes one argument and returns text.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. The hints come from other uses of Localize with a text key, so what the argument is here is not known.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the court position type into a script scope, so script values and script functions can be used on it.
details: The game lists it as a promote function (it changes what kind of object you hold). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the same name on other types is used to start a script call such as a script value.

label: Open appoint window
summary: Opens the window for appointing someone to this court position.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click in the court positions window and passes the owner of the court, whose court the appointment is for.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The owner of the court the appointment is for.

label: This position type
summary: The court position type itself, to hand it on as an argument.
details: Vanilla uses it in the court task window, for example to compare it with the selected position and to look up a character's aptitude for the position.

label: Toggle automation
summary: A command that switches the automation of this court position.
details: Vanilla checks it with IsValidCommand to enable a button and sends it with PostCommand when the button is clicked, in the appoint window and the court positions window. Which automation it switches to is not stated.

label: This window
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court positions window itself.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other windows use a function of the same name to pass themselves on.

label: Court owner
summary: The character who owns the court the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it in the window's texts, for example "Vacant ... in your court", to ask the owner for the right word for positions.

label: Expense breakdown
summary: The breakdown of what the court positions cost, for the expense part of the window.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a part of the court positions window.

label: Income breakdown
summary: The breakdown of what the court positions bring in, for the income part of the window.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a part of the court positions window.

label: Card background alpha
summary: How see-through the background of a position card is, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the alpha (opacity) value of a widget in the court positions window.

label: Court owner
summary: Going by its name, the character who owns the court shown.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; it uses CourtOwner instead. Other windows use a function of this name for the same idea.

label: Court positions
summary: The list of court positions the window shows.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of the main part of the court positions window.

label: Denied court positions
summary: The list of court positions that are denied (not available) in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it as a list in the window and hides that section when the list is empty. Why they are denied is not stated.

label: Group title
summary: The title text of a group of positions in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a group heading in the court positions window.

label: Held positions
summary: The list of court positions that are held (filled) in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it as a list in the window and hides that section when the list is empty.

label: Has employed positions
summary: Whether the court has any positions that someone holds.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the court positions window only when it is true.

label: Has empty positions
summary: Going by its name, whether the court has positions that nobody holds.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

label: This window
summary: Going by its name, the court positions window itself.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other types use a function of this name to pass themselves on as an argument.

label: Total earned salaries
summary: The total salary the court owner earns from holding court positions, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the label "Your Salary:", only when the court owner holds a court position, with the income breakdown as its data.

label: Total paid salaries
summary: The total of the monthly salaries paid out for the court positions, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it under the heading "Monthly Salaries:" in the court positions window, in a block that appears only when some positions are employed. The numbers come from the expense breakdown.

label: Scene artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts placed in the court scene, for the editor's artifact list.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of a part of the court scene editor window.

label: Scene assets
summary: The list of assets placed in the court scene, for the editor's asset list.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of a part of the court scene editor window.

label: Scene cameras
summary: The list of cameras of the court scene, for the editor's camera list.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of a part of the court scene editor window.

label: Scene characters
summary: The list of characters placed in the court scene, for the editor's character list.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of a part of the court scene editor window.

label: Scene lights
summary: The list of lights of the court scene, for the editor's light list.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of a part of the court scene editor window.

label: This window
summary: Going by its name, the court scene editor window itself.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. Other windows use a function of this name to pass themselves on as an argument.

label: Shadow camera of light
summary: The shadow camera that belongs to a given light, used as the data context of a part of the editor.
details: Vanilla passes the light of the current list row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The light whose shadow camera is wanted.

label: Editor toolset
summary: The toolset object of the court scene editor, used as the data context of a part of the window.
details: What the toolset holds is not stated beyond that use.

label: Add artifact
summary: Adds a new artifact to the court scene being edited.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the editor.

label: Add asset
summary: Adds a new asset to the court scene being edited.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the editor.

label: Add camera
summary: Adds a new camera to the court scene being edited.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the editor.

label: Add character
summary: Adds a new character to the court scene being edited.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the editor.

label: Add light
summary: Adds a new light to the court scene being edited.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the editor.

label: Can change active camera
summary: Whether the editor currently lets the user switch the active camera.
details: Vanilla uses it to fade out and disable the camera controls when it is false, together with the toolset being enabled.

label: Can redo
summary: Whether there is an undone change in the editor that can be redone.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the redo button.

label: Can undo
summary: Whether there is a change in the editor that can be undone.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the undo button.

label: Collapse all artifacts
summary: Folds all artifact entries in the editor's list to their short form.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Collapse all assets
summary: Folds all asset entries in the editor's list to their short form.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Collapse all cameras
summary: Folds all camera entries in the editor's list to their short form.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Collapse all characters
summary: Folds all character entries in the editor's list to their short form.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Collapse all lights
summary: Folds all light entries in the editor's list to their short form.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Duplicate artifact
summary: Makes a copy of the given artifact in the court scene.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the artifact's row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the artifact settings of the row, ArtifactSettings.Self

label: Duplicate asset
summary: Makes a copy of the given asset in the court scene.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the asset's row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the asset settings of the row, AssetSettings.Self

label: Duplicate camera
summary: Makes a copy of the given camera in the court scene.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the camera's row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the camera of the row, Camera.Self

label: Duplicate character
summary: Makes a copy of the given character in the court scene.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the character's row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the character properties of the row, CharacterProperties.Self

label: Duplicate light
summary: Makes a copy of the given light in the court scene.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click in the light's row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: the light of the row, Light.Self

label: Expand all artifacts
summary: Opens all artifact entries in the editor's list to show their settings.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Expand all assets
summary: Opens all asset entries in the editor's list to show their settings.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Expand all cameras
summary: Opens all camera entries in the editor's list to show their settings.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Expand all characters
summary: Opens all character entries in the editor's list to show their settings.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Expand all lights
summary: Opens all light entries in the editor's list to show their settings.
details: Vanilla calls it on a button click.

label: Active scene settings
summary: The scene settings set that is currently active in the editor.
details: Vanilla reads the visual culture from it for the line "Visual culture: ...".

label: Active settings index
summary: The position of the active settings set in the editor's list of sets.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected index of a list, so the active set is highlighted. It is returned as a two-number vector type.

label: All scene settings
summary: The list of all scene settings sets the editor knows.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data list of the settings selector.

label: Artifact description
summary: The description text of the given artifact in the scene.
details: Vanilla shows it as the artifact's row text.

label: Artifact description or slot
summary: The artifact's description, or, going by its name, its slot when there is no description.
details: Vanilla shows it as the artifact's row text. The fallback is read from the name.

label: Artifact locator
summary: The locator (attachment point in the scene) the given artifact is placed at, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the artifact's settings.

label: Artifact position
summary: One coordinate of the artifact's position in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three position fields.

label: Artifact rotation
summary: One rotation value (around one axis) of the artifact in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three rotation fields.

label: Artifact slot type
summary: The slot type of the given artifact (where it is worn or kept), as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the artifact's settings.

label: Asset description
summary: The description text of the given asset in the scene.
details: Vanilla shows the word 'Asset' when this text is empty.

label: Asset locator
summary: The locator (attachment point in the scene) the given asset is placed at, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the asset's settings.

label: Asset name
summary: The name of the given asset, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the asset's settings.

label: Asset position
summary: One coordinate of the asset's position in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three position fields.

label: Asset rotation
summary: One rotation value (around one axis) of the asset in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three rotation fields.

label: Asset scale
summary: The size factor of the given asset in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a slider and as its text.

label: Camera description
summary: The description text of the given camera.
details: Vanilla shows the word 'Camera' when this text is empty, and the royal court window shows it for the current camera.

label: Camera far limit
summary: How far the given camera sees, as a number (its far clipping distance).
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider's maximum, value and text. The "far clipping" reading comes from the name.

label: Camera field of view
summary: The field of view of the given camera, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and its text. Reading it as a field of view comes from the name.

label: Camera name key
summary: The localization key of the given camera's name, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the camera's settings.

label: Camera near limit
summary: How close the given camera starts to see, as a number (its near clipping distance).
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider's minimum, value and text. The "near clipping" reading comes from the name.

label: Camera position
summary: One coordinate of the camera's position in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three position fields.

label: Character description
summary: The description text of the given character entry in the scene.
details: Vanilla shows the word 'Character' when this text is empty.

label: Character locator
summary: The locator (attachment point in the scene) the given character stands at, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the character's settings.

label: Character position
summary: One coordinate of the character's position in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three position fields.

label: Character roles
summary: The roles of the given character in the scene, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the character's settings. What counts as a role is not stated.

label: Character rotation
summary: One rotation value (around one axis) of the character in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three rotation fields.

label: Light color
summary: The color of the given light, as a four-number color value (red, green, blue, alpha).
details: Vanilla uses it as the color of a swatch for a light in the editor. The name appears in other places too, so only this use is certain.

label: Light inner cone angle
summary: The inner angle of the given light's cone, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. It matters for spot lights; that reading comes from the name.

label: Light outer cone angle
summary: The outer angle of the given light's cone, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. It matters for spot lights; that reading comes from the name.

label: Current camera
summary: The camera that is currently in use in the court scene.
details: Vanilla passes it to GetCameraDescription for a debug line "Current Camera: ..." in the royal court window.

label: Light intensity
summary: How bright the given light is, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text.

label: Light description
summary: The description text of the given light.
details: Vanilla shows the word 'Light' when this text is empty.

label: Light intensity variation
summary: How much the given light's brightness varies, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text, in the settings of an animated light. Going by the name, it is the size of the flicker.

label: Intensity variation frequency
summary: How fast the given light's brightness varies, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Going by the name, it is the speed of the flicker.

label: Light look-at
summary: Going by its name, one coordinate of the point the given light is aimed at, as a number.
details: Vanilla never uses it, so this rests on the name alone.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the light (from the name only).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Presumably which axis (from the name only).

label: Light pitch
summary: The up-down aiming angle of the given light, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Reading it as the up-down angle comes from the name.

label: Light position
summary: One coordinate of the light's position in the scene, as a number.
details: Vanilla asks for 'x', 'y' and 'z' to fill the three position fields.

label: Light position variation
summary: How much the given light's position moves, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Going by the name, it is the size of the movement of an animated light.

label: Position variation frequency
summary: How fast the given light's position moves, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Going by the name, it is the speed of the movement.

label: Light type
summary: The type of the given light (such as its kind of light source), shown as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the light's settings. Which types exist is not given in the input.

label: Light yaw
summary: The left-right aiming angle of the given light, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Reading it as the left-right angle comes from the name.

label: Camera pitch
summary: The up-down aiming angle of the given camera, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Reading it as the up-down angle comes from the name.

label: Light radius
summary: The reach of the given light, as a number (its radius).
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text.

label: Camera shadow fade
summary: A shadow fade value of the given camera, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. What it fades is read from the name only.

label: Shadows fade
summary: The scene's general shadow fade value, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. It takes no argument, so it is not tied to one light or camera.

label: Shadows strength
summary: How strong the scene's shadows are, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. It takes no argument, so it is not tied to one light.

label: Editor toolset
summary: Going by its name, the toolset object of the court scene editor.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it uses AccessToolset instead. This rests on the name alone.

label: Camera yaw
summary: The left-right aiming angle of the given camera, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as a slider value and text. Reading it as the left-right angle comes from the name.

label: Light casts shadows
summary: Whether shadows are used for the given light.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the shadow settings of a light only when true, and as a tick box. The wording is read from the name.

label: Is animated light
summary: Whether the given light is animated (its brightness or position varies).
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box and to show the variation settings only for such lights.

label: Artifact expanded
summary: Whether the given artifact's entry is opened in the editor list.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the arrow frame of the entry and to show its settings only when open.

label: Asset expanded
summary: Whether the given asset's entry is opened in the editor list.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the arrow frame of the entry and to show its settings only when open.

label: Camera active
summary: Whether the given camera is the active one.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state in the camera's settings.

label: Camera is default
summary: Whether the given camera is the default one.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state in the camera's settings.

label: Camera expanded
summary: Whether the given camera's entry is opened in the editor list.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the arrow frame of the entry and to show its settings only when open.

label: Camera idle animation
summary: Whether the camera is animated while idle.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state. Reading it as a camera movement while nothing happens comes from the name.

label: Camera transition animation
summary: Whether camera changes are animated (a smooth move instead of a cut).
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state. The smooth-move reading comes from the name.

label: Camera used for screenshots
summary: Whether the given camera is the one used to take screenshots of the scene.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state and to show a marker in the camera's entry.

label: Character expanded
summary: Whether the given character's entry is opened in the editor list.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the arrow frame of the entry and to show its settings only when open.

label: Cubemap shadow
summary: Whether the given light uses a cubemap shadow.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state, together with the light's shadow setting. What a cubemap shadow is (a shadow cast in all directions) is read from the name.

label: Developer camera active
summary: Whether the free developer camera is switched on in the editor.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state, and a click switches it with SetDeveloperCameraActive.

label: Light enabled
summary: Whether the given light is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state and to show a marker in the light's entry.

label: Light expanded
summary: Whether the given light's entry is opened in the editor list.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the arrow frame of the entry and to show its settings only when open.

label: Light within limits
summary: Whether the given light stays within the allowed limits.
details: Vanilla shows a warning part when it is false. Which limits (such as a count of lights) is not stated.

label: Light shadow within limits
summary: Whether the given light's shadow stays within the allowed limits.
details: Vanilla shows a warning part when it is false. Which limits is not stated.

label: Show shadow camera
summary: Whether the debug view of the given light's shadow camera is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state next to the light's shadow setting. The shadow camera link is read from that use.

label: Show debug light
summary: Whether the debug display of the given light is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tick box state in the light's settings.

label: Toolset enabled
